podcast.body: Released in November 1979, this song from *The Wall* went to number one on the *Billboard* Hot 100 in March 1980. Roger Waters wrote the lyrics reflecting on 1950s British grammar schools, which he felt focused "more about controlling boys than educating them." The song, featuring a children's chorus and a "disco" sound, caused controversy, with some US teachers calling for it to be banned from radio, some stations resisting its play, and an outright ban in South Africa. A syndicated article by William Sebert in the *Cedar Rapids Iowa Gazette* (July 1980) highlighted the song's "uncommon and unsettling enthusiasm" among students who were questioning education and aware of cutbacks in youth services. "We don't need no education. We don't need no thought control. No dark sarcasm in the classroom teacher. Leave those kids alone. Hey, teacher, leave those kids alone. All in all it's just ain't another brick in the wall."

This song was one of the most popular singles of 1980, ranking higher than Olivia Newton-John's "Magic," but not as high as Blondie's "Call Me." "The third most popular single of 1980 came in behind Call Me by Blondie and another brick in the wall by Pink Floyd."
